steps: Confirm stock is checked in and sellable before the launch date.
Confirm the automatic PPC campaign is ready to start on launch day.
Confirm audience assets (waitlist, social, seeded creators) are ready to activate.
Flip the offer start date and activate everything the same day.

test.method: Track sessions, unit session percentage and review count in the first 2 weeks against a launch with less concentration.

title: Build an audience (waitlist, social, seeded creators) before launch day, not after
hypothesis: If we build an email waitlist, social following and seeded creator posts before launch day, then launch-week sales velocity improves because there is a ready audience instead of starting from zero on day one.

signal.check: A launch date is approaching with no email waitlist, social presence, or seeded creator content built yet.

expected_effect.size: example: 85 boxes seeded in one launch; influencer sweet spot 5,000 to 10,000 followers for free-product collaborations

risk.note: Never ask for a review or offer any incentive when seeding product to creators.

steps: Post the product's development story on the brand's own channels 6 to 8 weeks out.
Open an email waitlist and a small pre-launch feedback group.
Seed product to creators in the 5,000 to 10,000 follower range for honest posts, with no review ask or incentive.
Prepare a launch-day email and post using the built list.

test.method: Track launch-week sales and review count against the size of the pre-built audience.

title: Launch one SKU first; add colour or size variants only when the category requires them
hypothesis: If we launch one SKU first and add variants only when the category genuinely requires them (like apparel sizing), then launch cost and complexity fall because unnecessary colour or size variants split limited launch budget and attention.
does_not_apply_when: the category requires variants, such as apparel sizing, to be sellable at all

signal.check: A first launch plan includes multiple colours or sizes without a category requirement forcing variants.

expected_effect.size: one reported case: colour variants at launch cost about $2,500

risk.note: Apparel sizing is a real exception, not a mistake, when the category requires it.

steps: Check whether the category requires variants to be sellable (for example, apparel sizing).
If not required, launch a single SKU first.
Add colours, sizes or bundles later once the first SKU is proven.

test.method: Compare launch cost and cash needed for a single-SKU launch vs a multi-variant one.

title: Use only compliant launch levers; drop manual review generation from the plan
hypothesis: If we build the launch plan only from compliant levers (social, waitlist, influencers, Amazon Live, automatic PPC, launch-week discounting through Amazon's own tools) and drop manual review generation, then account risk falls because that one tactic breaches Amazon's terms.

signal.check: The launch plan includes any form of manual review generation, incentive, or recruiting alongside the compliant levers.

expected_effect.size: unknown, ecomOS rule and the source's own card reject the tactic

risk.note: None; removing a non-compliant tactic only reduces account risk.

steps: List every planned launch lever.
Keep only compliant ones: social media, email waitlist, a feedback group, influencer seeding with no review ask, Amazon Live, automatic PPC, and Amazon's own launch-week discount tools.
Remove any manual review generation, incentive or recruiting tactic.
Log the rejected tactic and why in the launch plan.

test.method: Confirm the final launch plan contains zero non-compliant review tactics.

title: Use price as an inventory throttle only when selling faster than the next delivery can restock
hypothesis: If we raise price as a throttle only under real stockout risk, then a stockout is avoided or delayed without cutting price into a healthy launch just to slow sales for no reason.
does_not_apply_when: stock cover is healthy and no stockout risk exists

signal.check: Sales velocity is outpacing the next delivery date, and price has not been considered as a throttle.

expected_effect.size: example: sales stayed steady across 2 price increases in one reported case

risk.note: A price change is an account write; a named human makes the change, not the agent.

prerequisites: stock cover and reorder timeline known
steps: Check remaining stock cover against the next delivery date.
If a stockout is likely before restock, raise price in steps as a throttle.
Have a named human make the price change; watch sales response after each step.

test.method: Track days of stock remaining and sales velocity after each price step.
test.read_point: weekly during a stockout risk period

title: Recover a stalled launch by reading sessions, unit session percentage and search terms before re-testing
hypothesis: If we read sessions, unit session percentage and the search term report before re-testing images or price on a stalled launch, then the fix targets the real problem because blind changes waste time on the wrong lever.

signal.check: A launch did not take off and the next step is to relaunch or edit the listing without first reading the traffic and conversion data.

expected_effect.size: unknown, single source, thin on method

risk.note: None; a diagnosis step before making changes.

prerequisites: at least 2 to 4 weeks of live sessions data
steps: Pull sessions and unit session percentage for the stalled listing.
Pull the PPC search term report for converting and non-converting terms.
Diagnose whether the problem is traffic (sessions) or conversion (unit session percentage).
Re-test the main image or price based on the diagnosis, not a guess.

test.method: Track unit session percentage before and after the targeted fix.

title: Route Amazon buyers to email or DTC with a packaging insert or QR code that carries no review ask
hypothesis: If we route Amazon buyers to the brand's email list or DTC site through a clean packaging insert or QR code, then owned-channel reach grows because Amazon otherwise keeps the buyer relationship entirely on-platform.
does_not_apply_when: the brand has nowhere yet to send the buyer, such as no email capture or DTC site

signal.check: FBA shipments go out with no packaging insert or QR code directing buyers to email or DTC, and the brand has an email list or DTC site to route them to.

expected_effect.size: unknown, general practice

risk.note: Word the insert to stay clear of any review ask or incentive; that risks a policy breach.

prerequisites: email capture or DTC site to route to
steps: Design a packaging insert or QR code that routes to email signup or the DTC site.
Write the wording with no review ask and no incentive.
Track the Attribution link (see the Brand Referral Bonus idea) for any tracked external routing.
Add the insert to the next production or repack run.

test.method: Track email signups or DTC visits attributed to the insert.

title: Protect a novel product with Brand Registry, Transparency and IP filing, not launch speed alone
hypothesis: If we protect a novel product with Brand Registry, Transparency and IP filing instead of relying on launch speed, then copycat risk falls because no evidence shows launch velocity alone prevents copying.
does_not_apply_when: product is not novel or easily copied

signal.check: A novel product's only planned protection against copycats is launching fast and loud, with no Brand Registry, Transparency or IP filing in progress.

expected_effect.size: unknown, no source shows launch speed alone blocks copying

risk.note: None; this adds protection rather than removing anything.

prerequisites: Brand Registry active or in progress
steps: File the trademark and enrol in Brand Registry.
Set up Transparency if hijack or counterfeit risk exists.
File a provisional patent for a genuinely novel product.
Do not rely on launch speed alone to prevent copying.

test.method: Track copycat listings or hijack attempts against the protections in place.

title: Run an automatic Sponsored Products campaign first to discover converting search terms
hypothesis: If we run an automatic campaign first before building manual campaigns, then wasted manual campaign spend falls because automatic targeting discovers which search terms actually convert before money is committed to guessed keywords.
does_not_apply_when: the SKU already has keyword performance history from a prior campaign

signal.check: PPC is being set up with manual keyword campaigns before any automatic campaign has run to discover converting terms.

expected_effect.size: unknown, a sequencing method

risk.note: None; this is campaign sequencing.

prerequisites: PPC budget set (see PPC budget idea)
steps: Create a Sponsored Products campaign with automatic targeting.
Set the daily budget from the PPC budget model.
Let it run for 2 to 4 weeks to gather search term data before building manual campaigns.

test.method: Compare cost per acquisition of terms found via automatic targeting vs guessed manual terms.
test.read_point: after 2 to 4 weeks of automatic data

title: Split the automatic campaign into 4 ad groups by targeting type with separate bids
hypothesis: If we split the automatic campaign into close match, loose match, substitutes and complements ad groups with separate bids, then PPC efficiency improves because a single blended bid overpays on low-intent traffic and underpays on high-intent traffic.

signal.check: The automatic campaign is running as one ad group with one blended bid instead of 4 targeting-type ad groups.

expected_effect.size: example bids: close $0.92, loose $0.72, substitutes $0.13, complements $0.71 (not benchmarks)

risk.note: The example bids are one product's numbers, not benchmarks; set bids from the brand's own data.

steps: Create 4 ad groups within the automatic campaign: close match, loose match, substitutes, complements.
Set a separate bid per ad group based on the brand's own margin and CPC data.
Allow dynamic bids down at launch, or up and down once margin allows.

test.method: Compare cost per acquisition by targeting group after the split.

title: Build manual keyword campaigns from proven search terms after 2 to 4 weeks of automatic data
hypothesis: If we build manual keyword campaigns from terms with actual orders in the automatic campaign's search term report, then PPC spend concentrates on proven converters instead of guessed keywords.

signal.check: Manual keyword campaigns are being built from a research tool's keyword list instead of the automatic campaign's own converting search terms.

expected_effect.size: filters used in one source's demo: under 5,000 monthly searches, 2+ words, 100 or fewer competing products, 2+ keyword sales a month

risk.note: Treat the filter values as a starting point to adapt, not a fixed rule.

prerequisites: 2 to 4 weeks of automatic campaign search term data
steps: Pull the search term report and keep terms with actual orders.
Filter additional keyword candidates for reasonable volume, word count, competition and keyword sales.
Build ad groups by match type: exact for proven converters, phrase and broad for discovery, each with negatives.

test.method: Track cost per acquisition for manual campaigns against the prior automatic-only period.

title: Run product targeting on weaker or higher-priced competitor ASINs, one ad group per competitor
hypothesis: If we run product targeting with one ad group per competitor ASIN, then profitability is readable per competitor because a blended campaign hides which competitors are worth targeting.

signal.check: Product targeting campaigns are blending multiple competitor ASINs into one ad group instead of separating by competitor.

expected_effect.size: unknown, a campaign structure method

risk.note: None; a campaign structure change.

steps: Identify competitor ASINs with a weaker listing or a higher price.
Create one ad group per competitor brand.
Review profitability per ad group and pause underperforming competitor targets.

test.method: Track cost per acquisition and orders by competitor ad group.

title: Add negative keywords to every live campaign from day one
hypothesis: If we add negative keywords to every campaign from day one, especially broad and phrase match, then wasted PPC spend falls because those match types are prone to matching irrelevant searches without them.

signal.check: A live campaign, especially one using broad or phrase match, has no negative keywords added.

expected_effect.size: unknown, mandatory practice with broad or phrase match

risk.note: None; negatives only reduce wasted spend.

steps: Add negative keywords for wrong formats, sizes or uses at campaign creation.
Review the search term report weekly and add new negatives for terms with spend and no orders.
Apply negatives at the campaign or ad group level as appropriate.

test.method: Track wasted spend (spend with zero orders) before and after adding negatives.

title: Judge PPC on net profit, not sales, and test reducing budget once organic momentum exists
hypothesis: If we judge PPC by net profit instead of sales volume and test reducing budget once organic sales hold, then overall profit rises because PPC-driven sales can mask an unprofitable acquisition cost.

signal.check: PPC performance is being judged by total sales or ACOS alone, without checking net profit after PPC spend.

expected_effect.size: one reported case: turning PPC down in month 6 caused a slight sales dip but profit rose

risk.note: An overspending, unprofitable campaign is the real risk this idea catches; test changes gradually and track net profit, not just ACOS.

prerequisites: organic sales history of at least a few months
steps: Compute net profit after PPC spend, not just ACOS or total sales.
Once organic sales are meaningful, test a lower PPC budget for a set period.
Compare net profit before and after the test.
Keep or reverse the change based on net profit, not sales alone.

test.method: Compare net profit for periods with different PPC budget levels.

title: Diagnose an ineligible-to-advertise listing by isolating the trigger, stripping description then images
hypothesis: If we isolate the ad-ineligibility trigger by stripping the description first, then removing images one by one, then PPC can restart faster because the flagged element is found instead of guessed.

signal.check: A listing cannot advertise and no systematic diagnosis has been run to find which element triggered it.

expected_effect.size: unknown, single source's diagnostic method, not guaranteed

risk.note: This is a diagnostic, not a guaranteed fix; check the current ad policy for the category as well.

steps: Check the live ad policy for the product's category.
Strip the description to a minimal, compliant version and re-check eligibility.
If still ineligible, remove images one at a time and re-check after each.
Restore the version once the eligibility check passes.

test.method: Track time to restore ad eligibility using this method vs guessing.

title: Add Sponsored Display or DSP retargeting once Sponsored Products is proven
hypothesis: If we add Sponsored Display or DSP retargeting once Sponsored Products is proven, then conversion from warm traffic improves because shoppers who viewed but did not buy get recaptured instead of lost.
does_not_apply_when: listing has too little traffic yet to build a meaningful retargeting pool

signal.check: Sponsored Products is profitable and stable but no retargeting layer exists for shoppers who viewed without buying.

expected_effect.size: unknown, no library source, verify against brand data

risk.note: DSP needs separate access beyond standard Seller Central; confirm eligibility and access first.

prerequisites: enough traffic for a retargeting pool
steps: Confirm Sponsored Products is profitable and has run long enough to build a viewer pool.
Check eligibility and access for Sponsored Display or Amazon DSP.
Set up a retargeting campaign for listing viewers who did not purchase.
Track its return separately from prospecting campaigns.

test.method: Track ROAS on the retargeting campaign against the prospecting campaigns.

title: Set the negative-keyword spend threshold from the brand's own margin, since no universal number exists
hypothesis: If we set the spend-with-no-orders threshold for negatives from the brand's own margin instead of a borrowed number, then PPC waste is cut correctly because no source gives a universal spend threshold.

signal.check: The weekly PPC review is using a guessed or borrowed spend threshold for adding negative keywords instead of one derived from the brand's own margin.

expected_effect.size: unknown, the source gives no threshold; must be set from brand data

risk.note: None; this sets a number the sources never provide.

steps: Compute the acceptable cost per click before a term is unprofitable, from unit margin and target conversion rate.
Set that as the spend threshold for adding a negative keyword with zero orders.
Apply the threshold in the weekly PPC review.

test.method: Track PPC spend efficiency after applying the brand-specific threshold.

title: Request reviews only through Amazon's permitted request path, without selecting only satisfied buyers
hypothesis: If we use only Amazon's permitted review-request path on every eligible order without hand-picking satisfied buyers, then review count grows without account risk because this is the only path every source agrees is compliant.

signal.check: Review requests are being sent manually or only to buyers believed to be satisfied, instead of through Amazon's own request tool on every eligible order.

expected_effect.size: one source reports an automated request about 5 days after delivery

risk.note: None; using the permitted path only reduces risk.

steps: Use Amazon's request-a-review button or automated tool on every eligible order.
Do not filter to only buyers believed to be satisfied.
Do not send any request outside Amazon's own permitted tool.

test.method: Track review count growth using the compliant path only.

title: Never reimburse, gift, or recruit friends or family for reviews, or link a refund to a review change
hypothesis: If we remove every incentive, gift, gating or recruited-reviewer tactic from the review process, then account suspension risk falls because these tactics breach Amazon's terms even when a source describes them as common.

signal.check: The current or planned review process includes any reimbursement, gift, gating, recruiting of friends or family, or a refund linked to a review change.

expected_effect.size: unknown, ecomOS rule; one source's own card agrees

risk.note: None; removing a risky tactic only reduces risk.

steps: Review the current review-request process for any incentive, gift, gating, or recruited reviewer.
Remove every such tactic immediately.
Document the removal and the reason so it is not reintroduced later.

test.method: Confirm zero incentivised, gated or recruited reviews appear in the review process.

title: Use Vine only under current terms and only once the product is genuinely ready
hypothesis: If we use Vine only under its current terms and only when the product is fully ready, then rating risk falls because a Vine reviewer outside the target audience or on an unready product can lower the rating.
does_not_apply_when: brand is not yet Brand Registered or the product is still being iterated

signal.check: Vine enrolment is being considered for a product still being finalised, or the current program terms have not been checked.

expected_effect.size: one reported case cost about $4,000+ from Vine reviewers outside the target audience

risk.note: Vine can lower the rating if the product or audience match is wrong; check current terms before enrolling.

steps: Check current Vine terms and eligibility.
Confirm the product is fully finalised and represents the brand well.
Enrol only when both conditions hold.
Accept that Vine can affect the rating either way.

test.method: Track rating change after Vine reviews post.

title: Contest seller feedback that is really a product review within 30 days, without offering any benefit
hypothesis: If we contest misplaced product-review feedback within Amazon's 30-day window and never offer a benefit for its removal, then unfair account-level feedback is cleared without breaching policy.

signal.check: Seller feedback that is really about the product, not the seller's service, has not been contested within the 30-day window.

expected_effect.size: unknown, a compliance process step

risk.note: Never negotiate removal with a benefit; that itself breaches policy.

steps: Check the current feedback removal rules.
Identify seller feedback that is actually a product complaint, not a service complaint.
Contest it through Feedback Manager within 30 days.
Never offer a refund, gift or discount tied to removing the feedback.

test.method: Track successful contest rate within the 30-day window.
test.read_point: within 30 days of the feedback appearing

title: Watch Amazon Account Health weekly for order defect rate, claims and policy notices
hypothesis: If we check Account Health weekly for order defect rate, negative feedback, A-to-z claims, chargebacks and policy notices, then account suspension risk falls because these metrics are the early warning before a suspension.

signal.check: No weekly process exists for checking the Account Health dashboard.

expected_effect.size: one healthy example showed 0% defects over 743 orders

risk.note: None; a monitoring habit.

steps: Open the Account Health dashboard weekly.
Check order defect rate, negative feedback, A-to-z claims, chargebacks and any policy notices.
Act on each notice immediately rather than letting it accumulate.

test.method: Track order defect rate and open policy notices week over week.

title: Run a full policy compliance audit covering barcodes, ship-from address, accounts and shared devices
hypothesis: If we run a combined audit of barcode source, ship-from address, account count and device or network sharing with reviewer accounts, then account suspension risk falls because each of these is independently flagged across sources as a suspension trigger.

signal.check: No single audit checks barcode source, ship-from address truth, account count and device or network sharing together.

expected_effect.size: unknown, a consolidated compliance check

risk.note: None; an audit, not a change.

steps: Confirm all barcodes are GS1, not gray-market.
Confirm the true ship-from address is used on every shipment.
Confirm no undisclosed duplicate seller accounts exist.
Confirm no shared devices or networks with any reviewer or seeded-creator accounts.

test.method: Track compliance audit pass rate quarterly.

title: Monitor Brand Registry alerts for hijackers and open a case immediately
hypothesis: If we monitor Brand Registry alerts for unauthorised sellers on the brand's ASINs and open a case immediately, then hijacker damage (price undercutting, counterfeit risk, lost Buy Box) falls because early action limits the window they can sell in.
does_not_apply_when: brand is not yet Brand Registered

signal.check: Brand Registry Alerts or the listing itself shows an unknown seller on the brand's ASIN with no case opened yet.

expected_effect.size: unknown, a monitoring and response habit

risk.note: None; earlier action only reduces damage.

steps: Check Brand Registry Alerts regularly for unauthorised sellers on the brand's ASINs.
Open a Brand Registry case immediately when one appears.
Use Transparency codes if counterfeit risk is present.

test.method: Track hijacker incidents and time-to-resolution.

title: Assign a named human owner for every Amazon account-changing action
hypothesis: If we assign a named human owner for every price, budget, shipment confirmation and publish action, then account mistakes and unauthorised writes fall because no automated process touches the live account without a person checking it.

signal.check: An Amazon account-changing action (price change, budget change, shipment confirmation, publish) has no named human owner assigned.

expected_effect.size: unknown, an ecomOS governance rule

risk.note: None; this is a governance control, not a live account change.

steps: List every action type that changes the live Amazon account: price, budget, shipment confirmation, listing publish.
Assign a named person as the owner for each action type.
Require that person's sign-off before any agent-drafted change goes live.
Log who approved each change.

test.method: Confirm every account-changing action in the log has a named human approver.

title: Send 3 to 6 months of stock cover per inbound shipment; smaller for an unproven SKU
hypothesis: If we send 3 to 6 months of cover per shipment once velocity is proven, and a smaller first batch for an unproven SKU, then both stockouts and long-term storage fees fall because either extreme (too little or too much) has a documented cost.

signal.check: A reorder or first order size is being set without checking it against proven sales velocity and MOQ constraints.

expected_effect.size: 3 to 6 months of cover is a repeated heuristic; one case shipped 100% of a large order and paid long-term storage plus about $1,300 to remove stock

risk.note: MOQ can force a larger first batch than ideal; drip a large run into FBA in tranches rather than sending it all at once.

prerequisites: sales velocity or a demand estimate
steps: For an unproven SKU, order the smallest run the MOQ allows that covers the launch window plus one reorder lead time.
Send it to FBA in tranches rather than all at once.
Once velocity is known, move to 3 to 6 months of cover per order.
Reorder when remaining cover hits 2 to 3 months.

test.method: Track stockout days and long-term storage fees against the order sizing rule used.

title: Treat a stockout as the failure mode to avoid; reorder early and rush if velocity rises
hypothesis: If we treat a stockout as the priority failure mode and reorder early or rush when velocity rises, then lost sales and rank drops fall because stockouts are reported as the single most expensive recurring mistake.

signal.check: Sales velocity is rising faster than the current reorder timeline accounts for.

expected_effect.size: reported losses across cases from about $5,000 to over $100,000 from stockouts

risk.note: Rushing an order costs more (expedited freight); weigh that against the reported cost of a stockout.

steps: Track weekly sell-through velocity against the reorder trigger.
If velocity rises faster than the current order and lead time can cover, place a rush reorder even at higher freight cost.
Treat a stockout as more costly than most rush-freight premiums.

test.method: Track stockout days per SKU per year against velocity-triggered rush reorders.

title: Watch inventory age and act before the long-term storage threshold hits
hypothesis: If we watch inventory age and act (sell through faster, request removal, or accept the fee) before the long-term storage threshold, then storage cost stays predictable because the threshold varies by source and is easy to miss.

signal.check: A SKU's inventory age is approaching a long-term storage threshold with no removal, discount, or acceptance decision made.

expected_effect.size: threshold reported as 365 days, 180 days, or 'beyond 6 months' depending on the figure

risk.note: Plan to the shortest stated threshold (180 days) until a live figure is confirmed, since that is the conservative side.

steps: Check the live long-term storage threshold for the marketplace.
Track inventory age per SKU against that threshold.
Before the threshold, choose: sell through faster (price or promotion), request removal, or accept the fee if removal costs more.

test.method: Track long-term storage fees paid against the age at which action was taken.

title: Plan Q4 stock early, accounting for about 3x normal volume and slower check-in
hypothesis: If we plan Q4 stock early with a roughly 3x normal volume estimate and a longer check-in window, then Q4 stockouts fall because both demand and processing time are reported to shift in that quarter.

signal.check: Q4 reorder timing is being planned the same as the rest of the year, without adjusting for higher demand and slower check-in.

expected_effect.size: presenter estimate: Q4 volume about 3x normal; check-in up to a month vs 1 to 2 weeks outside Q4

risk.note: The 3x figure is a presenter estimate; use the brand's own prior-year Q4 data if it exists.

steps: Pull the brand's own prior Q4 sales if available, or use the 3x estimate as a starting point.
Order Q4 stock earlier than the standard reorder trigger to allow for slower check-in.
Budget for the higher October to December storage rate.

test.method: Compare Q4 stockout days and storage costs against the plan.

title: Fetch current IPI, storage and restock limits live before planning inventory
hypothesis: If we fetch current IPI score, storage limits and restock limits live before planning inventory, then inventory plans stay realistic because none of these figures are covered in the source material and Amazon can cap how much stock is allowed in.

signal.check: An inventory or replenishment plan is being built without checking the account's current IPI score, storage limit or restock limit.

expected_effect.size: unknown, no source covers these figures; must be fetched live

risk.note: None; a live check before planning.

steps: Check the current Inventory Performance Index (IPI) score in Seller Central.
Check current storage and restock limits for the account.
Plan order sizes and reorder timing within those live limits.

test.method: Confirm the replenishment plan stays within the live storage and restock limits each quarter.

title: Use the Restock Inventory widget's days-of-supply estimate as a starting point, not the final answer
lever: restock widget as a starting estimate
hypothesis: If we use Amazon's own Restock Inventory widget for a days-of-supply estimate as a starting point, then replenishment planning starts from a live, account-specific number instead of a generic rule of thumb.

signal.check: Replenishment quantities are set from a generic rule of thumb without checking Amazon's own Restock Inventory widget.

expected_effect.size: unknown, a planning tool, not a measured result

risk.note: Treat the widget's suggested quantity as a starting point; adjust for known upcoming demand changes (promotions, Q4).

steps: Open the Restock Inventory widget in Seller Central.
Note the days-of-supply estimate and suggested reorder quantity.
Adjust that suggestion for any known upcoming demand change before finalising the order.

test.method: Compare actual days of supply against the widget's estimate after the order arrives.

title: Flag inventory approaching 150 days as an early warning before the long-term storage threshold
hypothesis: If we flag inventory approaching 150 days in the monthly report, then action happens before the long-term storage fee hits because a 150-day flag gives a buffer ahead of even the shortest stated threshold.

signal.check: The monthly report does not flag inventory age until it has already crossed a long-term storage threshold.

expected_effect.size: unknown, a buffer set ahead of the shortest stated 180-day threshold

risk.note: None; an earlier warning flag in existing reporting.

steps: Pull inventory age by SKU in the monthly report.
Flag any SKU approaching 150 days as an early warning.
Decide on sell-through, removal, or acceptance before it reaches the live long-term threshold.

test.method: Track how many SKUs reach the long-term threshold despite the 150-day flag.

title: Read sessions and unit session percentage separately before diagnosing a sales change
hypothesis: If we read sessions and unit session percentage separately every week, then the real cause of a sales change is found because traffic can rise while conversion falls (or the reverse) with total sales masking either move.

signal.check: Sales changes are being read from total revenue or orders alone, without splitting sessions from unit session percentage.

expected_effect.size: unknown, a diagnostic discipline

risk.note: None; a reading habit, not a change to the account.

steps: Pull sessions and unit session percentage weekly, not just total sales.
Check which one moved when total sales changes.
Diagnose a traffic problem (sessions) separately from a conversion problem (unit session percentage).

test.method: Track diagnostic accuracy: whether the identified cause (traffic or conversion) matched the fix that worked.

title: Track off-Amazon ad attribution before trusting its return
hypothesis: If we track off-Amazon ad spend to Amazon sales with Attribution links before trusting its reported return, then wasted ad spend falls because untracked spend can look productive while mostly not converting.

signal.check: Off-Amazon ad spend (social, search) directed at the Amazon listing has no Attribution tracking in place.

expected_effect.size: one reported case: Facebook spend was mostly wasted until tracking existed

risk.note: None; this is a measurement fix before trusting the spend.

prerequisites: Brand Registry enrolment for Attribution access
steps: Set up Attribution links for every off-Amazon channel sending traffic to the listing.
Track actual Amazon conversions from that tracked traffic.
Compare tracked return against the assumed return before committing more budget.

test.method: Compare tracked ROAS from Attribution against the previously assumed return.

title: Map revenue by month for a full year before calling a product a failure
hypothesis: If we map revenue by month across a full year before calling a product a failure, then good products are not killed early because an apparent decline can be ordinary seasonality rather than a real failure.

signal.check: A product's revenue dip is being read as failure without checking whether the same dip occurred in the same month a year earlier.

expected_effect.size: one reported case: a January dip was seasonal, not a failure

risk.note: None; a reading discipline before making a kill decision.

prerequisites: at least 12 months of sales history, where available
steps: Map monthly revenue for the product across the full year.
Check whether the same month showed a similar dip in a prior year.
Only call a product a failure after ruling out ordinary seasonality.

test.method: Track how many 'failing' products recovered in the following month once seasonality passed.

title: Use Amazon's own coupons, Lightning Deals and Prime Day, but never below the margin gate
hypothesis: If we use Amazon's own coupon, Lightning Deal and Prime Day tools for launch or clearance while keeping the 30% net margin gate, then promotional lift is captured without a promotion quietly turning a SKU unprofitable.

signal.check: A promotion (coupon, Lightning Deal, Prime Day) is being planned without checking the discounted price against the 30% net margin gate.

expected_effect.size: unknown, no source in this folder covers these tools directly

risk.note: None; the check is against a promotion that already erodes margin below the gate.

prerequisites: margin model for the discounted price
steps: Model the discounted price for the planned promotion.
Check that discounted price still clears the 30% net margin gate.
Use Amazon's own coupon, Lightning Deal or Prime Day tools rather than an off-platform discount scheme.
Track sell-through and margin during and after the promotion.

test.method: Compare net margin during the promotion period against the 30% gate.
test.read_point: during and 30 days after the promotion

title: Add a second ASIN only once the first hero SKU has proven sell-through and cleared the margin gate
hypothesis: If we add a second ASIN only once the first hero SKU has proven sell-through and clears the margin gate on its own, then portfolio cash risk falls because a second launch's budget and PPC reserve are sized separately, not borrowed from an unproven first SKU.
does_not_apply_when: the first SKU has not yet proven sell-through or cleared the 30% margin gate

signal.check: A second ASIN launch is being planned while the first hero SKU has not yet proven sell-through or a clean 30% net margin.

expected_effect.size: unknown, no source covers sequencing a second ASIN once the first is proven

risk.note: None; this only delays a second launch until the first is de-risked.

prerequisites: first SKU clears the 30% margin gate
steps: Confirm the first hero SKU has proven, repeatable sell-through.
Confirm it clears the 30% net margin gate on its own numbers.
Size the second launch's cash and PPC budget separately, not by assuming leftover capacity from the first.

test.method: Track cash and margin health of the first SKU before greenlighting the second ASIN's budget.
test.read_point: before committing to a second ASIN

title: Master a task yourself before outsourcing it, but delegate non-revenue admin work early
hypothesis: If we learn each Amazon task ourselves before hiring it out, while delegating non-revenue admin work early, then outsourced work is judged correctly because the founder can tell good work from bad only after doing it once.

signal.check: A task (listing build, PPC, sourcing follow-up) is being outsourced before anyone on the team has done it directly, or non-revenue admin is being kept in-house long after it should be delegated.

expected_effect.size: unknown, contrasted lessons from two sources

risk.note: None; a sequencing habit for hiring and delegation decisions.

steps: Do each core task (listing, PPC setup, sourcing follow-up) yourself at least once before hiring it out.
Identify non-revenue admin tasks (data entry, filing, basic reporting) and delegate those early.
Keep judgement calls on strategy and money in-house longer.

test.method: Track quality of outsourced work against whether the founder had done the task first.

title: Delay buying paid Amazon tools until there is enough sales data for them to act on
hypothesis: If we delay buying paid tools like reimbursement software or repricers until there is enough sales data for them to work on, then wasted subscription spend falls because these tools need volume to be worth their cost.
does_not_apply_when: the brand already has enough sales volume and data for the tool to act on

signal.check: A paid Amazon tool subscription is being bought before there is meaningful sales, review or fee data for it to work on.

expected_effect.size: unknown, sequencing lesson from one source

risk.note: None; delaying a subscription costs nothing but the manual work it would have automated.

steps: List paid tools under consideration (reimbursement software, repricers, research tools).
Check whether current sales volume and data justify the tool's cost.
Delay the subscription until volume or data reaches a point where the tool earns its cost back.

test.method: Track subscription cost against time-to-payback once each tool is adopted.

title: Set a growth or planned decline target once a revenue goal is hit, instead of coasting
hypothesis: If we set a next growth target or a deliberate decline plan once a revenue goal is hit, then a slow, unplanned decline falls because coasting after a goal is reported as one of the most expensive mistakes.

signal.check: A brand hit its Amazon revenue goal and has not set a new growth target or a deliberate maintenance plan.

expected_effect.size: unknown, presenter's own characterisation of the mistake

risk.note: None; a planning step once a goal is reached.

steps: Check whether the brand has a plan for after the current revenue goal is hit.
Set either a new growth target (new ASIN, new channel) or a deliberate plan to hold steady.
Avoid letting the business coast with no next target.

test.method: Track revenue trend in the months after a goal is hit against whether a next-step plan existed.

title: Account for about 2 months of manufacturing and freight lead time when judging a trending product
hypothesis: If we account for about 2 months of manufacturing and freight lead time before betting on a trending product, then dead stock from a faded trend falls because the trend may be gone by the time stock actually arrives.

signal.check: A trending product is being sourced without checking whether the trend is likely to still be relevant after about 2 months of manufacturing and shipping.

expected_effect.size: presenter reasoning: about 2 months manufacture and ship is the reason to avoid fads

risk.note: None; a timing check before committing to a trend-driven product.

steps: Estimate total manufacturing and freight lead time for the candidate product.
Judge whether the trend is likely to still be relevant in that many months.
Reject the candidate as a first launch if the trend looks unlikely to last that long.

test.method: Track sell-through of trend-driven launches against the lead time estimated at screening.

title: Write a one-page Amazon channel decision memo before deciding to add the channel
hypothesis: If we write a one-page channel decision memo with every gate result and sourced number before deciding to add Amazon, then the decision is defensible and repeatable because it is not based on memory or a gut call.

signal.check: A yes, no, or not-yet decision on adding Amazon is being made without a written memo covering the gate results and their sources.

expected_effect.size: unknown, a documentation discipline

risk.note: None; documentation only, the memo itself is advisory.

steps: Run the channel fit checklist and the fee and margin model on the brand's own numbers.
Write the recommendation (yes, no, not yet) with the date.
List gate results: category, trademark, price floor, net margin, cash, differentiation, fulfilment fit.
List open web checks and brand-data gaps still outstanding.
Name the human owner for each next step.

test.method: Confirm the memo exists and every number in it traces to brand data, a quote, or a dated web check.

title: Fund the first production run with a pre-order crowdfunding campaign, not personal capital
hypothesis: If we fund the first production run through a pre-order crowdfunding campaign instead of the founder's own capital, then launch capital risk falls because backers pay before manufacturing starts and cash is not tied up in speculative stock.
does_not_apply_when: the product cannot be demonstrated with a prototype or has no story or audience to rally around it

signal.check: A new, untested product needs a first production run and the founder has little capital to risk on unsold inventory.

expected_effect.size: unknown, source cases raised from about $1,500 up to over $100,000 across two campaign rounds

risk.note: A failed or under-funded campaign delays the launch and is public. Back it with a real prototype and an existing audience, not just an idea.

prerequisites: some audience or content channel to drive traffic to the campaign
steps: Build a low-cost prototype, even a paper or hand-made sample, to show in the campaign.
Set the funding goal against the next specific cost, such as a design deposit or the first production run.
Launch the campaign on a pre-order platform and drive traffic from the brand's own content and audience.
Fulfil backers directly once the run is manufactured, then send remaining stock into FBA.

test.method: Track campaign funding against the goal and compare the effective cost of this capital against a loan or self-funded run.

title: Ask a manufacturer for a referral to cover a production step they cannot do themselves
hypothesis: If we ask an existing manufacturer for a referral when they cannot handle a production step, then finding a trustworthy second vendor takes less time, because a referral already carries some vetting.

signal.check: A manufacturer can do part of the production, such as blending, but not another part, such as packaging.

expected_effect.size: unknown

risk.note: A referral still needs its own vetting before a production order.

prerequisites: an existing relationship with a primary manufacturer
steps: Ask the primary manufacturer directly whether they know a vendor for the step they cannot cover.
Request contact details or a direct introduction rather than starting a cold search.
Vet the referred vendor the same way as any new supplier before committing.
Note the referral source in the supplier record for future sourcing.

test.method: Compare time to first usable quote for a referred vendor against a cold-sourced vendor on a comparable gap.
test.read_point: once the second vendor is confirmed

title: Run a tracked, mass cold-outreach campaign to 50 or more manufacturers for a hard-to-source product
hypothesis: If we send one templated outreach message to 50 or more manufacturers and track replies in a spreadsheet, then we find a willing supplier for a novel product faster, because most manufacturers refuse a new process and a handful of contacts is not enough.
does_not_apply_when: a standard, widely-manufactured product where a normal Alibaba or ThomasNet search already returns willing suppliers

signal.check: Normal supplier search returns mostly refusals for a novel product or an unusual manufacturing process.

expected_effect.size: unknown, one case found 1 to 2 willing suppliers out of 50 to 60 contacted

risk.note: Time cost only. Treat a refusal call as free technical education to refine the pitch for the next batch.

prerequisites: a list of 50 or more candidate manufacturers, including results beyond the first page of search
steps: Write one outreach template describing the product and the ask.
Build a list of 50 or more candidate manufacturers, paging well past the first page of search results.
Send the same template to every contact and log outreach and replies in a spreadsheet.
Call any manufacturer who refuses to learn their technical reason and refine the pitch for the next batch.
Follow up with every willing respondent on minimum order quantity, lead time and options.

test.method: Track reply rate and number of willing suppliers found per 50 contacted.
test.read_point: after the full contact list is worked

title: Ask a manufacturer making an adjacent product for a free leftover sample to prototype cheaply
hypothesis: If we ask a manufacturer already producing something adjacent for a free leftover or blank sample instead of commissioning a custom one, then prototype cost falls, because we pay only shipping instead of a full custom production run.
does_not_apply_when: the product needs a fully custom mould or spec with no adjacent product to draw a sample from

signal.check: A product idea needs a physical prototype before validating demand or running a crowdfunding campaign, and no sample exists yet.

expected_effect.size: about $50 in shipping only, in one sourced example

risk.note: A leftover sample may not exactly match the final spec. Treat it as a directional prototype, not a production-ready sample.

prerequisites: a manufacturer identified who makes a similar or adjacent product
steps: Search a supplier directory for a manufacturer making an adjacent, not exact, version of the product.
Ask if they have a leftover or blank sample from a past project and request it, offering to pay shipping only.
Use the sample to build a prototype, pitch deck or crowdfunding campaign visual.
Commission a custom sample only once demand looks real.

test.method: Compare cost and time to first prototype using this method against commissioning a custom sample directly.
test.read_point: once the prototype is in hand

title: Widen manufacturer search to supplier databases, trade shows, directories and agents when Alibaba stalls
hypothesis: If we widen manufacturer search beyond Alibaba and direct outreach to supplier-lookup databases, trade convention exhibitor lists, regional B2B directories and paid sourcing agents, then we find a willing manufacturer faster, because each channel reaches a different pool of suppliers.
does_not_apply_when: a standard product where Alibaba search already returns several qualified, willing suppliers

signal.check: Alibaba search and direct cold outreach have not produced a qualified, willing manufacturer.

expected_effect.size: unknown

risk.note: A sourcing agent or concierge service carries a fee. Confirm current pricing before committing.

steps: Search a supplier-lookup database by competitor ASIN or company name to see who manufactures a similar product.
Search for the product's industry trade conventions and contact or attend the exhibitor list of a relevant show.
Search a regional B2B directory if sourcing outside Alibaba's main pool.
Consider a paid sourcing agent or concierge service to search and vet suppliers directly.
Log every new lead the same way as an Alibaba lead for vetting.

test.method: Track the number of qualified leads found per channel used.

title: Negotiate manufacturer price with a volume-commitment quote and by citing a competing offer
hypothesis: If we ask for pricing at a large target volume and then cite a competing supplier's quote, then per-unit cost falls, because manufacturers price more aggressively for a larger eventual order and to win against a named competitor.
does_not_apply_when: a manufacturer with fixed, non-negotiable published pricing

signal.check: A shortlisted manufacturer's first quote has not been tested against a larger volume ask or a competing quote.

expected_effect.size: unknown

risk.note: Only quote a volume the store genuinely intends to reach eventually.

steps: Ask for pricing at a large target volume the store genuinely intends to reach eventually.
After the quote, ask to start with a smaller test order and see if the manufacturer holds the quoted rate.
Tell the manufacturer the specific per-unit price another shortlisted supplier quoted and ask if they can match or beat it.
Weigh any price win against quality and reliability before deciding, not on price alone.

test.method: Compare the final negotiated per-unit price against the manufacturer's first quoted price.

title: Ask the manufacturer to execute product design changes before hiring a separate CAD designer
hypothesis: If we describe a product change directly to the manufacturer first, then design cost falls, because most manufacturers can execute a described or sketched change themselves as part of their normal service.
does_not_apply_when: the manufacturer states the change is outside their capability

signal.check: A product needs a design or dimension change and the default plan is to hire an outside CAD designer first.

expected_effect.size: unknown

risk.note: Asking first costs nothing and does not block hiring a designer afterward if needed.

steps: Describe the desired change in words and simple sketches to the manufacturer.
Ask directly whether they can execute it as part of their normal service.
Hire an outside CAD designer only if the manufacturer says the change is outside their capability.
Confirm the final design with a sample before the bulk order.

test.method: Track design cost and turnaround time using this sequencing against hiring a CAD designer first.

title: Test converting an existing FBM SKU to FBA and measure the sales change from Prime eligibility
hypothesis: If we convert an existing FBM SKU to FBA and measure the before-and-after sales change, then we learn whether Prime eligibility is driving a sales gap on that SKU, because Prime badge and delivery speed are reported to lift conversion meaningfully.
does_not_apply_when: the SKU is already on FBA
a product too heavy, fragile or made-to-order for FBA economics

signal.check: An existing FBM SKU sells below what its traffic or category would suggest, and it has not been tested on FBA.

expected_effect.size: source claims several times more sales after conversion in one case; unverified for other products

risk.note: FBA fees replace FBM shipping cost. Model both before committing stock to the change.

prerequisites: an existing FBM listing with some sales history
steps: Record the FBM SKU's current sessions, conversion rate and monthly units.
Model FBA fees against the product's price and margin before converting.
Convert the fulfilment channel to FBA and send stock in.
Compare sessions, conversion rate and units for a comparable period after conversion.

test.method: Before-and-after comparison of conversion rate and units on the same SKU across an equal time window.
test.read_point: 30 days after the FBA listing goes live

title: Proactively contact a buyer behind a negative review or account defect to try to resolve it
hypothesis: If we proactively reach out to a buyer who left a negative review or an order defect to resolve the underlying issue, then order defect rate and average rating improve, because some buyers update or remove a complaint once the problem is actually fixed.
does_not_apply_when: the review or defect type breaches Amazon's own rules for seller-initiated contact on that case type

signal.check: A new negative review, defect or A-to-z claim appears with no outreach yet from the seller.

expected_effect.size: unknown

risk.note: Never offer a refund or incentive in exchange for changing or removing a review. Resolve the underlying issue only.

prerequisites: weekly Account Health and review monitoring already in place
steps: Check Account Health and new reviews weekly for a negative review or defect.
Contact the buyer through Amazon's permitted messaging channel to understand the issue.
Offer a genuine fix, such as a replacement or usage guidance, without asking for a review change.
Log the resolution and watch whether the rating or defect status updates.

test.method: Track review rating and order defect rate over the following month against the prior month.

title: Commission a factory audit or a sourcing-agent visit before a large order with an unfamiliar manufacturer
hypothesis: If we commission a factory audit or a local sourcing agent's visit before a large order with an unfamiliar overseas manufacturer, then fraud and quality risk falls, because a platform profile alone cannot confirm the supplier is a real factory or check labor conditions.
does_not_apply_when: a manufacturer with an established, multi-order track record with the brand

signal.check: A large first order is planned with a manufacturer in an unfamiliar country and no independent, in-person verification has happened.

expected_effect.size: unknown

risk.note: An audit or agent visit adds cost and lead time but is far cheaper than a failed production run or a labor-condition problem.

prerequisites: a shortlisted manufacturer with no prior order history
steps: Commission a factory audit covering production capability and labor conditions before a large order.
Or hire a local sourcing agent to physically visit and confirm the supplier is a real factory, not a reselling middleman.
Walk away from a manufacturer that scores poorly on the audit, regardless of price.
Record the audit or agent findings in the supplier file for future orders.

test.method: Track defect rate and delivery reliability on orders from audited versus non-audited new suppliers.
test.read_point: after the first large order is received

title: Ship the first production run to yourself first for a personal quality check before forwarding it to Amazon
hypothesis: If we ship the first production run to ourselves before sending it on to Amazon, then defective units reaching customers fall, because a personal check catches problems a photo report or a rushed inspection might miss.
does_not_apply_when: the manufacturer relationship is already established and a paid third-party inspection is already in place

signal.check: A first production run from a new or overseas manufacturer is about to ship straight to an Amazon warehouse with no personal check.

expected_effect.size: unknown

risk.note: Adds shipping time and cost against shipping direct to Amazon. Weigh this against launch date pressure.

steps: Ship the first production run to the founder or a trusted address instead of directly to Amazon.
Open and check a sample of units against the approved sample and the product brief.
Fix or reject the batch before it reaches Amazon if defects are found.
Repack and forward the approved units into the FBA inbound shipment.

test.method: Track return rate and 1 to 3 star review rate on self-checked shipments against direct-to-Amazon shipments.
test.read_point: 90 days after the shipment goes live for sale

title: Fund the first production run with a private investor for repayment plus a profit share
hypothesis: If we fund the first production run with a private investor who is repaid plus a share of ongoing profit, then the founder can launch without draining personal savings or waiting to save enough capital.
does_not_apply_when: the founder already has enough capital, or crowdfunding is a better fit for the product

signal.check: A validated product idea is stalled only by a lack of launch capital, and neither savings nor a loan is available or wanted.

expected_effect.size: unknown

risk.note: Put the profit-share agreement and repayment terms in writing, with real diligence, before accepting money from a private individual.

steps: Approach an individual investor, such as a friend, family member or relevant community, with the product idea and numbers.
Offer repayment of principal plus an agreed share of ongoing profit.
Put the agreement and repayment terms in writing before accepting funds.
Track and report actual results against the agreement.

test.method: Track whether the investor is repaid on schedule and compare the effective cost of this capital against a loan or crowdfunding.
test.read_point: once the investor is fully repaid

title: Enrol a qualifying low-price, lightweight SKU in Amazon's Small and Light program to cut the FBA fee
hypothesis: If we enrol an eligible low-price, lightweight SKU in Amazon's Small and Light program, then per-unit FBA fee falls, because that program's fee schedule runs lower than the standard tier for qualifying products.
does_not_apply_when: the SKU does not meet the program's current price, weight or dimension eligibility

signal.check: A low-price, lightweight SKU is on the standard FBA fee tier and has not been checked against Small and Light eligibility.

expected_effect.size: about $0.50 per unit in one cited example

risk.note: Program eligibility rules and pricing change. Re-check current terms before enrolling.

prerequisites: a SKU under the program's current price and weight limits
steps: Check the SKU's price, weight and dimensions against the current Small and Light eligibility rules.
Enrol the SKU in the program through Seller Central if eligible.
Compare the new per-unit fee against the standard tier fee.
Monitor for any change in delivery speed or customer experience after enrolling.

test.method: Compare per-unit FBA fee and net margin before and after enrollment.

title: Use Amazon's AI listing generator from an existing DTC product page instead of a blank new listing
hypothesis: If we paste an existing DTC product page URL into Amazon's new-listing flow instead of starting from a blank form, then listing build time falls, because the tool drafts title, description and attributes for editing rather than writing them from scratch.
does_not_apply_when: no existing DTC product page to draw from
the feature is unavailable in the current Seller Central account

signal.check: A new Amazon listing is about to be built from a blank form for a product that already has a live DTC product page.

expected_effect.size: unknown, feature availability and output quality need a live check

risk.note: Always edit the draft for keyword placement, benefit-led bullets and accuracy before publishing. Do not publish it unedited.

prerequisites: an existing DTC product page for the same product
confirm the feature is available in the current Seller Central account
steps: Confirm the AI listing generator is available in the current Add Products flow.
Paste the brand's own DTC product page URL when prompted.
Review the auto-generated draft title, bullets, description and attributes.
Rewrite the title and bullets for the target keyword and benefit-first copy before publishing.

test.method: Compare time spent building the listing this way against building one from a blank form.

title: Test the same logo brief across several design-sourcing price tiers before picking a designer
hypothesis: If we run one identical design brief across several logo-sourcing price tiers and always check portfolios first, then brand image quality per dollar improves, because output quality does not scale smoothly with price and the cheapest tier can still work if vetted.
does_not_apply_when: the brand already has an established, trusted designer relationship

signal.check: A new brand or product needs a logo and no design-sourcing comparison has been run yet.

expected_effect.size: unknown, one source's own 5-tier test ranged $10 to $900 for very different results

risk.note: A rejected logo at any tier costs only that tier's fee and time, not the whole budget.

prerequisites: one written brief covering the product, tone, 1 to 2 keywords and 2 to 3 preferred colors
steps: Write one identical brief covering the product, tone, keywords and colors.
Post it to at least 2 different price tiers, such as a freelance marketplace and a design contest platform.
Review each freelancer's portfolio before hiring, even at the cheapest tier.
Compare results and pick by output quality against the brief, not by price alone.

test.method: Compare cost per usable logo option across the tiers tested.
test.read_point: once a final logo is chosen

title: Run an Amazon Live stream demonstrating the product around launch day
hypothesis: If we run an Amazon Live stream demonstrating the product around launch day, then launch-week traffic and conversion improve, because a live demo adds a visible, interactive proof point competitors without one do not have.
does_not_apply_when: Amazon Live is not available for the seller's account or category

signal.check: A launch plan includes static content and ads but no live demonstration channel.

expected_effect.size: unknown

risk.note: Confirm current Amazon Live eligibility and format before planning the launch around it.

prerequisites: Amazon Live eligibility confirmed for the account
steps: Confirm the seller account is eligible for Amazon Live.
Plan a short demo script covering the product's main benefit and use case.
Schedule and promote the stream around the planned launch window.
Compare launch-week sessions and conversion against a prior launch without a live stream.

test.method: Compare launch-week sessions and conversion rate for a launch with an Amazon Live stream against one without.

title: Use your own Amazon Associates link on your own external traffic to recapture an affiliate commission
hypothesis: If we route our own external traffic to our Amazon listing through our own Associates affiliate link, then net acquisition cost falls, because we recapture a commission on top of the referral fee we already pay, on sales we drove ourselves.
does_not_apply_when: already enrolled in the Brand Referral Bonus Program for the same traffic, since the two may not stack

signal.check: External traffic from content, social or email is sent to the Amazon listing with a plain product link, not an Associates affiliate link.

expected_effect.size: about 5% cited in one case

risk.note: Confirm current Associates program terms and whether it can run alongside the Brand Referral Bonus Program before relying on both.

steps: Apply for or confirm an Amazon Associates account.
Generate an Associates link for the brand's own ASIN.
Replace plain product links with the Associates link in the brand's own external content and ads where allowed.
Check current program rules for whether this can run alongside the Brand Referral Bonus Program.
Track the resulting commission against the referral fee already paid.

test.method: Track affiliate commission earned on self-driven traffic over a month.
